bull.b: The Anthropic lease materially improves long-term revenue visibility and shifts the business toward contracted AI infrastructure income. Its 20-year term and major-customer relationship can support sustained capacity investment and reduce reliance on spot Bitcoin-mining economics.

bull.t: Growing HPC Platform and Power Access
bull.b: Secured power access is a durable competitive asset in AI data centers, where grid availability constrains growth. The approval supports execution of the Justified campus and strengthens TeraWulf's ability to convert contracted demand into operational capacity.

Substantial liquidity and proceeds from monetizing Abernathy provide funding for Lake Mariner, Justified, Muskie and Chesapeake commitments. Recycling capital toward larger controlled campuses may improve strategic focus and reduce dependence on near-term equity issuance.

bear.t: Persistent Losses and Weak Cash Generation
bear.b: The core business remains far from self-funding, with severe losses and substantial cash burn despite revenue growth. Continued investment and operating deficits increase reliance on financing, asset sales or additional capital before new HPC capacity generates returns.

Very high leverage relative to reported equity leaves limited balance-sheet flexibility and heightens refinancing and dilution risk. Debt-funded expansion may amplify shareholder exposure if project commissioning is delayed or contracted assets take longer to reach targeted economics.

bear.t: Execution Costs and Near-Term Margin Pressure
bear.b: Scaling AI infrastructure is currently consuming significant pre-revenue resources, while constrained electrical labor and customer-driven design changes create schedule risk. Until additional capacity comes online, low reported margins and negative EBITDA can pressure liquidity and returns.
